episodes.title: Aletta Jacobs
episodes.description: Vrouwenrechten, universiteitstoegang en stemrecht in Nederland

words.note: "In deze aflevering…" = "In this episode…" The speaker introduces the podcast topic: Aletta Jacobs.
Aletta Jacobs is beroemd in Nederland because she fought for women's rights.
From vechten = to fight. "Ze heeft gevochten voor de rechten voor vrouwen."
"Hiermee heeft ze Nederland veranderd" = "By doing this, she changed the Netherlands."

words.nl: wilde ze heel graag net zoals
words.en: she really wanted to, just like
words.note: "Ze wilde heel graag net zoals haar vader dokter worden" = she really wanted to become a doctor, just like her father.
"Om dat beroep te kunnen doen…" = "To be able to do that profession…" Here, the profession is doctor.
Women were expected to marry, have children, and do het huishouden: cleaning, cooking, caring for children.
"De macht van de adel en van de kerk werd steeds minder" = the power of the nobility and the church became weaker.
Men gained more rights and freedoms around the French Revolution — but women did not.
Dutch translation of the French slogan "liberté, égalité, fraternité."

words.nl: veranderde er weinig en ze kregen geen nieuwe rechten
words.en: little changed and they received no new rights
words.note: For women, the political changes of the French Revolution did not bring much progress.
"Verder studeren was niet toegestaan" = further study was not allowed for girls/women.
Many women worked until they got married — after which they were fired.

words.en: after that they were dismissed / fired
words.note: Women were often fired from their jobs after marriage — this was the norm.

words.nl: Mijn eigen oma heeft nog meegemaakt dat ze werd ontslagen toen ze trouwde met mijn opa
words.en: My own grandmother still experienced being fired when she married my grandfather
words.note: The speaker's personal example — this was not ancient history at all.

words.nl: Pas in 1955 werd het automatisch ontslag bij huwelijk uit de wet gehaald
words.en: Only in 1955 was automatic dismissal upon marriage removed from the law
words.note: Pas = only / not until. Uit de wet gehaald = removed from the law.
"Thorbecke is vooral bekend omdat…" = Thorbecke is especially known because…

words.nl: In arme gezinnen werkte de vrouw vaak wel, om rond te komen
words.en: In poor families, the woman often did work, to make ends meet
words.note: Rondkomen = to earn enough to live on.
"Er was nog geen bijstand vanuit de overheid" = there was not yet government welfare support.
Support coming from the state, as opposed to family, church, or charity.

words.en: everyone had to do their bit / contribute
words.note: Literally: contribute their little stone. Everyone had to help financially.
Thorbecke is known for writing the Dutch grondwet (constitution).

words.nl: een uitzondering krijgen op de regels
words.en: to get an exception to the rules
words.note: Aletta wrote to Thorbecke asking for an exception so she could study medicine.

words.en: so that she could study after all
words.note: Toch = after all / despite the obstacle. Zodat = so that, sending the verb to the end.

words.nl: vlak voor de dood van Thorbecke
words.en: shortly before the death of Thorbecke
words.note: Vlak voor = shortly before / just before. She received the exception just in time.
People worried about the aanwezigheid (presence) of a woman in university lecture halls.
Afleiden = to distract. The fear was that Aletta would distract the male students.
"Een jurk die niet opvalt" = a dress that does not stand out. She tried to blend in.
Aletta was gepest (bullied) by fellow students at university.
As a woman, she was often not taken seriously by professors and peers.
She continued despite the resistance and opposition she faced.
Few people used condoms or other voorbehoedsmiddelen at the time.
Repeated pregnancies were erg zwaar (very heavy/hard) for women's health and wellbeing.
Zogenaamde = so-called. A contraceptive device Aletta introduced to poor women for free.
Smaller families meant children could receive more care and attention.
Aletta's ideas about contraception and smaller families were vernieuwend (innovative) for the time.

words.en: the law stated / the law said
words.note: "In de Nederlandse wet stond…" = "In Dutch law it said…"

words.nl: In de wet stond namelijk niet dat dat niet zo was
words.en: After all, the law did not say that this was not the case
words.note: Aletta's clever argument: the law did not explicitly say women could not vote.

words.nl: Maar daar was niet iedereen het mee eens
words.en: But not everyone agreed with that
words.note: Officials and judges disagreed with Aletta's interpretation of the law.
The Dutch Hoge Raad is described as vergelijkbaar (comparable) to the US Supreme Court.
The judges ruled the law should be interpreted as allowing only men to vote.
"Het kiesrecht voor vrouwen" = women's suffrage, the right for women to vote.
Aletta wanted women to be able to vote in verkiezingen (elections).
In 1919, women in the Netherlands were officially allowed (toegestaan) to vote.
Aletta became voorzitter (chairperson) of the Vereeniging voor Vrouwenkiesrecht.
"Bepaalde onderwerpen" = certain topics, such as politics, were considered unsuitable for women.
Used in the old argument against women voting: what would happen if husband and wife voted differently?
Used ironically by the speaker — mocking the old argument that only men should vote to avoid conflict at home.

words.nl: Steeds meer mensen sloten zich bij hen aan om te vechten voor gelijke rechten
words.en: More and more people joined them to fight for equal rights
words.note: Zich aansluiten bij = to join. Gelijke rechten = equal rights.
From strijden = to fight/struggle. "Er werd gestreden voor vrouwenrechten."

words.en: boss of one's own belly / bodily autonomy
words.note: A feminist slogan from the second wave — women wanted control over their own bodies, including abortion and contraception.

words.en: bodily autonomy / control over one's own body
to be removed from the law

words.nl: een uitzondering krijgen op de regels
words.en: to get an exception to the rules

episodes.title: De elfstedentocht
episodes.description: De beroemde Friese schaatstocht: traditie, weer, en waarom heel Nederland meeleeft

sections.title: Intro: de tocht waar iedereen naar uitkijkt

words.note: Full phrase: "Er is een schaatswedstrijd in Nederland waar iedereen naar uitkijkt" = "There is a skating race in the Netherlands that everyone looks forward to."
The length and difficulty of the tour depend on the weather: cold, wind, and ice quality.
"Als het heel koud is, er veel wind is of slecht ijs is, is de elfstedentocht heel erg zwaar" = if it is very cold, windy, or the ice is bad, the tour is very tough.
This is Frisian, not standard Dutch. In Dutch it means "het gaat door." These are the famous words announcing that the Elfstedentocht will happen.
The voorzitter van de organisatie says "it giet oan" when the tour can go ahead.

words.nl: dat de tocht gereden werd sprak men van een Elfstedenkoorts
words.en: when the tour was held, people spoke of "Elfstedentocht fever"
words.note: Men sprak van… = "people spoke of…" / "it was called…" Koorts literally means fever, but here it means national excitement.
Not an illness, but a country-wide enthusiasm about the upcoming tour. Similar to Oranjekoorts for the Dutch national football team.

words.en: The whole Netherlands followed along / got emotionally involved
words.note: Meeleven means to emotionally follow something, sympathise, or be involved. Here it means the whole country shared the excitement.

sections.title: Ijs, klimaat en waarom de tocht zeldzaam is

words.note: Ice made artificially, for example in an ice rink.
Ice that forms naturally on canals, lakes, and rivers. The Elfstedentocht is skated on natuurijs, not artificial ice.
"De verwachting is dat…" = "The expectation is that…" The podcast says the expectation is that strict winters will become less common.

words.en: holes / open patches in the ice
words.note: Een wak is a large hole or open water spot in the ice. Too much wind can create wakken, making the route unsafe.
"Tegenwoordig is schaatsen vooral voor je plezier" = nowadays skating is mainly for fun.
In the past, skating was not only a sport; it was a practical vervoermiddel in winter if you did not have a horse.
"Waarschijnlijk is de tocht ontstaan…" = the tour probably started because of bets about who could visit all eleven cities in one day on skates.

words.en: so many people want to participate
words.note: So many people want to take part that there is a waiting list.
Used often for races, competitions, events, and activities.

words.nl: die starten het ook gaat lukken
words.en: those who start will also manage
words.note: Full idea: "dat zoveel mogelijk mensen die starten het ook gaat lukken om te finishen" = that as many people as possible who start will also manage to finish.
Very useful Dutch verb. Het lukt me = I manage / I succeed. Het gaat lukken = it will work out / they will manage.

words.nl: je ziet de naam 'Van Buren' bij een reservering, moet je even goed opletten!
words.en: if you see the name "Van Buren" on a reservation, you should pay close attention
words.note: Goed opletten = pay close attention. The joke is that "Van Buren" is a pseudonym used by members of the Dutch royal family.
Here, a restaurant reservation.
The podcast explains that Van Buren was used as a hidden name by Willem-Alexander.
"Wel honderdduizenden" people stand along the route to cheer on the skaters.

words.nl: gebruikt worden sluiten niet overal op elkaar aan
words.en: that are used do not connect everywhere
words.note: Full phrase: "De verschillende bevroren sloten, kanalen en meren die gebruikt worden sluiten niet overal op elkaar aan." The frozen waterways used for the route do not all connect neatly.

words.en: to connect to each other / join up
words.note: Useful phrase for physical connections, schedules, systems, or ideas.

words.nl: dat doe je met je schaatsen aan om niet te veel tijd te verliezen
words.en: you do that with your skates on so as not to lose too much time
words.note: This describes klunen: walking over land with skates on between pieces of ice.

words.nl: er worden matten neergelegd om de schaatsen te beschermen
words.en: mats are laid down to protect the skates
words.note: Neergelegd = laid down / put down. The mats stop the skate blades from being damaged when people walk over land.
A traditional Dutch soup made with split peas.
Snert is the informal/traditional name for Dutch pea soup, often eaten in winter.

words.nl: ten slotte nog één feitje om te laten zien hoe belangrijk het is
words.en: finally, one more little fact to show how important it is
words.note: Ten slotte = finally. Feitje = little fact. The speaker introduces a final example showing how important the Elfstedentocht is to Dutch people.

words.en: it is going ahead / it is happening
not just participate / not simply take part

words.nl: het gaat lukken om te finishen

words.en: to connect to each other / join up

words.nl: om niet te veel tijd te verliezen
words.en: so as not to lose too much time

words.note: Het gaat lukken = it will work out. Gaat het lukken? = will you manage? Het is me gelukt = I managed it.
